newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION - WORLD CHAMPS BEATEN BY STUDENT COUNTERPARTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - WORLD CHAMPS BEATEN BY STUDENT COUNTERPARTS.

text.p: World champions South Africa crashed to the second defeat of their tour of France on Tuesday, beaten 20-13 by their counterparts at university level.
South Africa, whose first string beat France 22-12 in the first test in Bordeaux on Saturday, lost their opening tour match 10 days ago against the French Barbarians.

The French University team, who won the world crown when they beat South Africa's students in a Johannesburg final in July, showed they could live with the best, fly-half David Aucagne securing victory with five penlties.
Inspired by the Barbarians' success, the students put up stern resistance against the strong Springbok pack and troubled the touring side when they played the ball out.

"We took them by storm and I hope we gave our elders a few ideas for Saturday," said the students' coach Christian Lanta, looking ahead to the second test between France and South Africa at the Parc des Princes in Paris.
Aucagne opened the score for the students with a penalty in the seventh minute, but his opposite number Franco Smith replied in kind six minutes later.
Rough forward exchanges dominated play until well after the half hour and the touring team showed slight superiority in this department by going ahead with another Smith penalty.

But the students' eforts to open the game out bore fruit when, six minutes before the interval, wing Jean-Marc Souverbie chased an astute kick ahead by flanker Arnaud Costes to touch down in the corner, giving them a 8-6 halftime lead.
The home side pulled further ahead with Aucagne's second penalty, then defended their lead resolutely against some driving play by the Springbok forwards.

After Aucagne's third penalty for the students, a fine try by replacement wing Joe Gillingham on the hour, following up his own chip ahead, and converted by Smith, brought South Africa right back into the game at only 14-13 down.
But the students, sensing an historic win, held firm and pulled further away with two more Aucagne penalties.
"They have a stereotyped game," said Aucagne. "To take them on, you have to press them. From the moment you put them under this prssure, they are in trouble and can't find a solution."

"We were troubled by the refereeing," said Springboks assistant coach Nick Mallett. "We were constantly harassed and getting our shirts pulled. The referee was not up to it (the occasion) but that's not the French team's fault. They played with bite and will. It's certainly a big disappointment."

French University selection: 15-Nicolas Brusque; 14-Frederic Tauzin, 13-Luc Lafforgue, 12-Fabrice Ribeyrolles, 11-Jean-Marc Souverbie; 10-David Aucagne, 9-Gregory Sudre; 8-Christophe Dongieu, 7-Serge Betsen, 6-Arnaud Costes, 5-Thierry Cleda, 4-Colin Gaston (19-Yann Lemeur 67), 3-Olivier Sourgens, 2-Raphael Ibanez (captain), 1-Olivier Azam (21-William Rebeyrotte 54).

South Africa: 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Justin Swart, 13-Jeremy Thomson, 12-Dick Muir, 11-Breyton Paulse (17-Joe Gillingham 52); 10-Franco Smith, 9-Roelof Viljoen; 8-Johan Erasmus, 7-Theo Oosthuizen, 6-Wayne Fyvie (captain), 5-Krynauw Otto, 4-Frederick van Heerden (19-Hannes Strydom 60), 3-Marius Hurter, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Gary Pagel.
